* Add serde-style annotations: alias, skip_serializing(_if), skip_deserializing, default_value, default_from, with, flatten, rename_all, deny_unknown_fields, transparent

Continues the C++26 annotation work (rename, skip) for issue #2660, adding the
serde attributes that make sense for C++ structs and enums. Adds the
UNKNOWN_FIELD error code for deny_unknown_fields.

* Fix review issues in serde-style annotations

- builder: when the buffer allocation fails, reset the writer to the
  string_builder's invalid state (null buffer, zero capacity and
  position). Callers of a failed ensure() only return from the current
  atom and their callers kept writing through the freed pointer (e.g.
  the closing '}' after atom_fields, or later keys after a flattened
  member).
- builder: call_through_string_builder is noexcept only when its
  callback is, so an exception thrown by a with<Adapter> serializer
  (including std::bad_alloc) propagates instead of calling
  std::terminate.
- with<Adapter>: a transparent structure read directly from a document
  silently bypassed an adapter taking an ondemand::value. The document
  is now converted with get_value() (a scalar document reports
  SCALAR_DOCUMENT_AS_VALUE; an adapter taking auto& receives the
  document). A deserialize function that cannot be called at all is a
  compile-time error instead of being ignored.
- Two members accepting the same JSON key (through rename, alias,
  rename_all or flatten) are a compile-time error: one key used to fill
  every member that listed it. This removes the duplicate_keys_fall_back
  test that checked that behaviour.
- Keys that the key_selector cannot take, and keys written with escape
  sequences (quote, backslash, control character), now go through a
  scan of the object that compares unescaped keys (shared with
  deny_unknown_fields), in the default and the opt-out builds. obj[key]
  compares raw bytes and never matched them.
- deny_unknown_fields: the keys of const and non-public members, which
  are serialized but not deserialized, are ignored rather than
  unknown, so a serialized value parses back.
- flatten on a string, container, optional, smart pointer or reference
  member is a compile-time error (a reference could make flattening
  cycle).
- Tests: the escaped-key test of deny_unknown_fields now uses an
  escaped key; new tests for escaped keys, round trips with
  deny_unknown_fields, adapters on transparent structures and throwing

entries.subject: Do not drop empty or duplicate keys in fractured_json table rows (#2908)
entries.message:
Do not drop empty or duplicate keys in fractured_json table rows (#2908)

When fractured_json lays out an array of objects as a table, it can lose
keys. With default options:

    fractured_json_string(R"([[{"":1}]])")         // [ [ {1} ] ]
    fractured_json_string(R"([[{"a":1,"a":2}]])")  // [ [ {"a": 1} ] ]

The first output is not valid JSON. The table code used an empty
table_column::key to mean "array row", so a column for the valid key ""
was written without its key and colon. Mark object columns with an
explicit has_key flag instead.

The second output silently loses "a":2. A table column holds one value
per row, so later duplicates of a key had nowhere to go. Duplicate names
are valid JSON (RFC 8259 only says they SHOULD be unique), and the DOM,
minify() and prettify() keep them. When a row has a duplicate key, do
not lay out the array as a table or as aligned compact rows, so the
regular formatter writes every member. Duplicates are detected by
recording the last row that filled each column, which adds no hashing
or per-row allocation.

Add regression tests for both cases.

entries.subject: Add support for C++ 20 ranges. (#1050)
entries.message:
Add support for C++ 20 ranges. (#1050)

C++ 20 adds a new feature called "ranges", which provides components for dealing
with sequences of values: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/ranges.

A range is like a normal object containing `begin` and `end`, except there are
also composable operations like maps, filters, joins, etc.
The iterator objects returned by a range's `begin` and `end` require a more
strict set of operations than is needed for a range-for loop.

This PR adds the extra operations needed to support turning `dom::array` and
`dom::object` into a range.
This PR does not depend on any C++ 20 behavior, the added operators are all
valid C++ 11, and are already part of the LegacyIterator concepts.
This PR adds extra code behind: `#if defined(__cpp_lib_ranges)` guards, which is
the new C++ 20 specified feature test macro for ranges support. When ranges
support is detected, extra compile time checks are added to ensure that
`dom::array` and `dom::object` satisfy the range concept. No runtime tests have
been added yet because these compile time checks should be sufficient.

If desired, the `static_assert` code could be moved out of the actual code
headers and put into a test file.

Add On-Demand getters for narrower integers and std::float32_t/std::float64_t (#2881)

get_uint8(), get_int8(), get_uint16() and get_int16() range-check
get_uint64()/get_int64() the same way get_uint32()/get_int32() already
do, and return NUMBER_OUT_OF_RANGE when the value does not fit. The

provides std::float32_t and std::float64_t. get_float32() parses with

entries.subject: Fix ambiguous atom()/append() on optional serialization (#2827) (#2828)
entries.message:
Fix ambiguous atom()/append() on optional serialization (#2827) (#2828)

Since C++26 (P3168), std::optional is itself a range, so
concepts::container_but_not_string matched std::optional. That made the
container and the optional overloads of builder::atom() and
builder::append() equally good candidates, and reflection-based
serialization of any struct holding an std::optional failed to compile
under GCC 16 with -std=c++26:

    error: call of overloaded 'atom(string_builder&,
      const std::optional<std::string>&)' is ambiguous

Master carried a partial fix (a !optional_type guard bolted onto the
atom() container overload), but the equivalent append() overload was
still ambiguous, so a top-level to_json(std::optional<T>) did not
compile either.

Fix the root cause instead: exclude optional types from
container_but_not_string, since an optional is never serialized as an
array. That covers every overload that keys off the concept, so the
bolted-on guard in atom() goes away.

Tests cover an optional as a struct member, as the top-level value, and
nested both ways with a vector, in both the reflection and the
non-reflection builder.

entries.message:
Arm64 sve runtime detection (#2867)

* arm64: runtime detection of SVE and SVE2

Add SVE and SVE2 bits to instruction_set and detect them at runtime on
AArch64: AT_HWCAP/AT_HWCAP2 via getauxval on Linux, and
IsProcessorFeaturePresent on Windows. Other systems report NEON only.
This is groundwork for SVE/SVE2 runtime dispatching; no kernel uses
the new bits yet.

* arm64: do not include <asm/hwcap.h> for SVE detection

The kernel UAPI header is not available on all toolchains (e.g., musl
without linux-headers). <sys/auxv.h> plus our fallback definitions of
AT_HWCAP2/HWCAP_SVE/HWCAP2_SVE2 are sufficient.

* arm64: require HWCAP_SVE before claiming SVE2

Before Linux 6.14, HWCAP2_SVE2 was set on processors implementing SME(2)
without SVE, since SVE2 instructions are available in streaming mode.
Gate SVE2 on SVE so we never select a non-streaming SVE2 kernel on such
systems.

entries.subject: Do not read past an empty JSON pointer in On-Demand at_pointer (#2912)
entries.message:
Do not read past an empty JSON pointer in On-Demand at_pointer (#2912)

object::at_pointer and array::at_pointer read json_pointer[0] before
checking the length. An empty pointer has no first character. With a
default-constructed std::string_view, data() is null, so this crashes:

    ondemand::object obj = doc.get_object();
    obj.at_pointer(std::string_view{});   // SIGSEGV at object-inl.h:304

With "" the read is still out of bounds: -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS aborts
with "Assertion '__pos < this->_M_len' failed". value::at_pointer reaches
the same code through get_object()/get_array().

Check for an empty pointer first. An object or array that has already
been started cannot be returned as a value, so they keep returning
INVALID_JSON_POINTER, as they already did for "". value::at_pointer("")
now returns the value itself, as RFC 6901 specifies and as
document::at_pointer("") already does.

entries.subject: fix wildcard path recursion depth (#2844)
entries.message:
fix wildcard path recursion depth (#2844)

for_each_at_path_with_wildcard() recurses once per path segment and never
checked the parser's depth limit. A long wildcard path applied to a deeply
nested document kept descending: with development checks it tripped the
max_depth assertion in set_start_position(), and in a release build it
exhausted the stack and crashed. Return DEPTH_ERROR instead.

entries.subject: Fix member initialization order warning in auto_parser
entries.message:
Fix member initialization order warning in auto_parser

The compiler was warning about member initialization order mismatch.
C++ initializes members in the order they are declared in the class,
not the order they appear in the initializer list.

Fixed by reordering member declarations to match the initialization
order needed: m_doc must be initialized before m_parser since we
need to call parser.iterate() before moving the parser.

This fixes the -Werror=reorder compilation error in CI.
